title: KV-aware Parameter Residency Manager playbook
body:
Purpose and scope
This doc proposes a pragmatic, incremental implementation for a parameter residency manager that is KV-cache-aware and kernel-affinity informed. The goal is to reduce tail latency and backend bandwidth during steady-state inference and cold-starts, avoid refetch storms, and make hot-swap safe for both hosted and private deployments. This is a playbook: patterns, invariants, rollout steps, and acceptance criteria rather than a finished spec.

Problem statement (observed pain)
- Large mixed-size models (dense transformer layers + large embedding tables) cause unpredictable memory pressure.
- Simple LRU/mmap heuristics lead to refetch storms when many requests share rare prefixes or long-context KV usage.
- Hot-swapping model versions can briefly corrupt KV cache affinity leading to increased 99.9th percentile latency.
- Kernel selection (FP16 vs int8 paths) benefits when contiguous layer ranges are resident; fragmented residency forces suboptimal kernel fallback.

Design principles
- Signal-driven: residency decisions should incorporate KV cache hit/miss telemetry and recent kernel execution patterns.
- Incremental rollout: keep conservative defaults; introduce aggressive eviction/placement only behind feature flags and metrics gating.
- Safe hot-swap: commit protocol with atomic activation + KV cache era tagging so in-flight requests can complete against prior residency view.
- Minimal locking on the fast path: lock-free residency lookups; background coordinator handles placement and evictions.

Concepts and components
- Residency Table (RT): in-memory structure mapping parameter segment id -> residency state {resident_shard_ids, mmap_file, version_tag, checksum}. Must be read-optimized (atomic reads).
- KV Telemetry Feed: compact event stream with keys: request_id, prefix_id, kv_accessed_segment_ids[], kernel_path_hint (e.g., fp16, int8), request_latency. Aggregated into hotness scores per segment.
- Placement Agent: background worker that consumes hotness scores and issues "load" operations (mmap, direct fetch) with priorities and prefetch windows.
- Eviction Controller: policy that considers current GPU memory utilization, predicted near-term hotness, and kernel affinity (prefer evicting isolated segments that don't break contiguous kernel-friendly groups).
- Atomic Activation Protocol: two-phase activation for model swaps: (1) prepare new RT snapshot and load prioritized segments; (2) flip active RT pointer atomically; (3) background finalization to populate remaining segments lazily. Each RT snapshot has an era id used by KV cache entries.

Signal model and priority scoring
- Hotness score = alpha * recency + beta * access_frequency + gamma * kv_hit_proportion + delta * kernel_affinity_bonus. Tunable weights.
- Kernel affinity bonus: if a segment is adjacent to N resident segments that share kernel path X, increase its score to avoid breaking the run.
- Cold-start prefetch: use model metadata to prefetch embedding tables and first L transformer block when sequence length > configured threshold.

Loading strategies
- mmap-first fallback: try platform mmap for large segments (>= 64MB) to avoid copying. On platforms without robust mmap, fall back to faulting reads.
- small-segment eager copy: for small parameters (< 1MB) prefer direct allocation and memcpy into pinned GPU buffers to avoid page table churn.
- streaming activation: for very large sharded models, stream the first N layers synchronously until they are resident; asynchronously stream remaining layers on demand.
- safetensors verification: verify checksum in RT before activation; if mismatch, quarantine file and signal fetch from artifact store.

Eviction heuristics
- Soft eviction: demote to mmap-backed residency (keep file on disk but free RAM) before full discard. This favors faster reactivation.
- Affinity-aware grouping: evict whole groups that are least recently used instead of scattered individual segments to preserve kernel-friendly contiguity.
- Reactive backpressure: if eviction throughput cannot keep up, temporarily reduce placement aggressiveness and increase prefetch latency budget.

KV cache coordination
- Era tagging: when RT flips (hot-swap), increment era. Each KV cache entry stores the era it was written against. On read, if era mismatch, mark stale and optionally rehydrate using the new RT; stale entries are evicted lazily.
- Per-prefix pinning: allow temporary pin of small high-value segments for certain prefix_ids to avoid repeated misses for known hot prefixes (configurable per-customer).

Hot-swap safety and rollback
- Prepare stage loads critical segments and runs a short health-check synthetic inference (local) to validate outputs against baseline thresholds. Health-check uses a fixed prompt set to catch gross regressions.
- Flip is an atomic pointer swap to a new RT snapshot. In-flight requests continue against previous RT (era). New requests see the new RT.
- Rollback path: if health-check fails or telemetry shows sudden spike in error/latency, perform atomic swap back to previous RT and mark the failed snapshot quarantined.

Metrics and SLOs to watch
- segment_miss_rate (per-segment and aggregated) — target: < 1% steady-state for hot segments.
- cold_start_time_95 — time for first successful token generated after model selection — target: reduce by 25% vs baseline.
- background_load_throughput — segments/sec.
- kernel_fallback_rate — percent of kernels picking fallback path due to fragmented residency — target: < 2%.
- eviction_reactivation_latency — median/99p time to reactivate an evicted segment.

Operational toggles and feature flags
- residency_v1 (current simple heuristics)
- kv_signal_prefetch (enable KV-driven prefetch)
- affinity_grouping (enable contiguous-group-preserving eviction)
- era_tagging (enable era-based hot-swap)

Rollout plan
1) Lab validation: implement RT and basic placement agent; run workload generator against synthetic models; validate metrics. (2 weeks)
2) Canary: enable in a single low-traffic region with kv_signal_prefetch disabled; verify no regressions for 1 week. (1 week)
3) Gradual enable kv_signal_prefetch and affinity_grouping behind 10/30/50/100% traffic gates with automated rollback on metric spikes. (2–4 weeks)
4) Enable era_tagging and hot-swap flows for non-critical customers; observe rollback rate and KV churn for 2 weeks. (2 weeks)
5) Wide rollout with monitoring and alerting thresholds.

Acceptance criteria before GA
- No increase in 99.9th percentile token latency across canary traffic.
- kernel_fallback_rate decreased or unchanged.
- segment_miss_rate for annotated hot segments reduced by at least 30% in steady-state tests.
- Successful hot-swap rollback tests pass without data corruption.

Open questions / TODOs
- Weighting of kernel_affinity_bonus needs experimental tuning. Suggested experiment: offline traces grouped by kernel path.
- How to surface per-customer pinning policy safely and with quotas? Design billing/limits.
- Interaction with Dedicated reserved capacity: should the placement agent honor capacity reservations differently? (likely yes)
- Exact threshold sizes for mmap vs eager copy are hardware dependent — add auto-calibration job.

Notes to implementers
- Keep the RT sharded by segment id to reduce contention; use atomic pointer swap for snapshots.
- Avoid large synchronous prefetches on hosts serving latency-sensitive traffic. Use background workers.
- Expose a diagnostic endpoint that can dump current RT snapshot + hotness scores for debugging.

Appendix: short sequence example (simplified)
- T0: model v1 active, era=42. Request R1 accesses prefix P and touches segments [s2, s3]. KV telemetry marks s3 hot.
- Background: placement agent increments score for s3, schedules mmap load for s3.
- T1: operator prepares model v2 snapshot; placement agent preloads [s0..s5]. health-check runs.
- T2: atomic swap to era=43. New requests see v2; KV cache entries still tagged era=42 are served for in-flight requests.
- T3: eviction controller demotes stale era=42 segments; era mismatch entries are lazy-evicted from KV cache.

References and pointers
- Runtime PR #482 (linked) – initial RT implementation prototype.
- ENG-9273 – ticket tracking experiments for kernel affinity scoring.

End of playbook.

Quick TODOs (owner-prefixed)

Comments welcome.
